51058385.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant heparanase catalytic stie (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface plasmon: All the surface plasmon resonance experiments were performed at room temperature using a Biacore T100 instrument. Diluted heparanase samples (50 μg mL−1) were prepared from concentrated stocks of the protein by adding 10 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH 5), and later immobilized on a carboxymethylated (CM5) sensor chip. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 150 mM NaCl, 50 μM EDTA, 0.005% surfactant P20. Activation of the sensor chip surface was performed with a mixture of N-hydroxysuccinimide (NHS, 115 mg mL−1) and 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC, 750 mg mL−1) for 7 min at 10 μL min−1. The amount of heparanase immobilized on the activated surface was 2400 RU. After immobilization of the protein, a 7 min injection (at 5 μL min−1) of 1 M ethanolamine (pH 8.5) was used to quench excess active succinimide ester groups. Surface plasmon resonance binding experiments were performed in the same running buffer used for heparanase immobilization plus 2% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to alleviate solubility problems of the compounds. The flow rate and the contact time were 30 μL min−1 and 120 s, respectively. Compound concentrations ranging from 5 μM to 1 mM were always used in these experiments. The sensor surface was regenerated between experiments using 10 mM glycine (pH 2.5) for 30 s at 30 μL min−1 to remove any complex formed. Analysis of the binding curves was performed with software provided by Biacore.

Bottom: superposition of the sensorgrams obtained after injection of amodiaquine at different concentrations.
original_paragraph.Figure 2b data: The bottom sensorgram in Figure 2b shows response curves for amodiaquine at concentrations of 300.0 μM, 100.0 μM, 50.0 μM, 25.0 μM, 12.5 μM, and 6.25 μM. The x-axis represents time in seconds (s), ranging from -100 to 800 s. The y-axis represents response in resonance units (RU), ranging from -100 to 600 RU. The top plot shows the response (RU) as a function of concentration (μM), with concentration ranging from 0 to 300 μM.
original_paragraph.Table 3: Table 3 lists the SPR results for the highest ranked compounds from the Prestwick Chemical Library. For Amodiaquine (Prest-542), the K_D value is 52.6 μM. For other compounds, K_D values are >1 mM or 1 mM.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - SPR experiments: SPR experiments were also carried out to determine the dissociation constants (K_D) of the selected set of compounds. It was found that amodiaquine displayed the highest affinity (K_D = 52.6 μM, Fig. 2b) of this set of chemicals, while the remaining six compounds exhibited K_D values in the order of 1 mM or above (Table 3). The affinity value found for amodiaquine was within the same order of magnitude of those measured by SPR (data not shown) for a subset of known inhibitors with IC_50s ranging from 0.23 to 25 μM.
